{
  "correction_rules": [
    "When sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 with recent downward drift), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish bias.",
    "If model forecast spikes sharply (e.g., >10% above recent high), apply a 5–10% downward correction to prevent overreaction.",
    "In periods with sustained positive sentiment (e.g., 0.50+), model forecasts tend to overestimate; apply a 3–7% downward adjustment to align with mean reversion.",
    "When true outcome deviates significantly from model (e.g., >10% error), check if sentiment history includes recent 0.00 or 0.33 — if so, apply a 5–10% downward bias correction.",
    "For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently overestimates in early days (e.g., days 1–5), reduce first 5 forecast points by 3–8% to account for lag and volatility.",
    "If sentiment history includes 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 2–5% upward adjustment to prevent underestimation.",
    "In cases where true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >10% increase from prior day), model often underestimates — apply a 3–7% upward bias to capture momentum."
  ]
}
